translations.text: ᚠ (feoh, wealth) is a comfort to every man.
Yet every man must share it out freely if he wishes to win glory before the Lord.
ᚢ (ur, aurochs) is fierce and great-horned, a very fierce beast; it fights with its horns, a famous moor-stalker; that is a brave creature.
ᚦ (Thorn) is very sharp. For every thane, taking hold of it is bad, and it is beyond measure cruel to any man who lies down among it.
ᚩ (os, mouth) is the source of all speech, the support of wisdom and the comfort of wise men, and a blessing and hope to every warrior.
ᚱ (rad, riding) is easy for every warrior in the hall, and very strenuous for the one who sits on a mighty horse over the long roads.
ᚳ (cen, torch) is known to every living person by its fire, pale and bright; it burns most often where princes rest indoors.
ᚷ (gyfu, gift) is an honour and praise to men, a support and a dignity, and to every outcast who has nothing else it is help and sustenance.
ᚹ (wynn, joy) is enjoyed by the one who knows little of woe, pain and sorrow, and who himself has prosperity and happiness and also plenty of strongholds.
ᚻ (hægl, hail) is the whitest of grains; it whirls down from the air of heaven, gusts of wind toss it about, and afterwards it turns to water.
ᚾ (nyd, need) is tight on the breast, yet it often becomes a help and a healing to the children of men, if they heed it in time.
ᛁ (is, ice) is very cold and extremely slippery; it glistens clear as glass, most like jewels, a floor made by frost, fair to look at.
ᛄ (ger, year) is the hope of men, when God, the holy King of heaven, lets the earth give bright fruits to rich and poor alike.
ᛇ (eoh, yew) is a tree rough on the outside, hard, fast in the earth, a keeper of fire, supported by roots, a joy on the estate.
ᛈ (peorth) is always play and laughter for the proud, where warriors sit happily together in the beer-hall.
ᛉ (eolhxsecg, elk-sedge) most often has its home in the fen; it grows in the water, wounds grimly, and burns with blood any man who makes any grab at it.
ᛋ (Sun) is always a hope to seafarers when they carry it over the fish's bath, until the sea-steed brings them to land.
ᛏ (tir) is a certain sign; it keeps faith well with princes; it is always on its course over the mists of night and never fails.
ᛒ (beorc, birch) bears no fruit, yet it bears shoots without seed; it is beautiful in its branches, high in its crown, finely adorned, laden with leaves, reaching to the sky.
ᛖ (eh, horse) is a joy to princes among warriors, a horse proud in its hooves, when heroes, wealthy men on steeds, exchange talk about it; and to the restless it is always a comfort.
ᛗ (man) in his mirth is dear to his kinsman; yet each one must fail the other, because the Lord by his decree will commit the wretched flesh to the earth.
ᛚ (lagu, water) seems endless to people if they must venture out on an unsteady ship, and the sea-waves terrify them greatly, and the sea-horse pays no heed to its bridle.
ᛝ (Ing) was first seen by men among the East Danes, until he later went back east over the wave; his wagon ran after him; so the Heardings named the hero.
ᛟ (ethel, homeland) is very dear to every man, if he may enjoy there in his house what is right and proper, most often in prosperity.
ᛞ (Day) is the Lord's messenger, dear to men, the glorious light of the Creator, a joy and a hope to rich and poor, of use to all.
ᚪ (Oak) on earth is food for the flesh of the children of men. It often travels over the gannet's bath, and the ocean tests whether the oak keeps noble faith.
ᚫ (Ash) is very tall and dear to men. It stands firm on its base and holds its place rightly, though many men fight against it.
ᚣ (Yr) is a joy and an honour to every prince and nobleman. It looks fine on a horse, is dependable on a journey, and is a piece of war-gear.
ᛡ (Ior) is a river-fish, and yet it always takes its food on land. It has a fair dwelling surrounded by water, where it lives in joy.
ᛠ (ear, the grave) is loathsome to every warrior, when the flesh, the corpse, steadily begins to grow cold and, pale, to choose the earth as its bedfellow; fruits fall, joys pass away, pledges fail.
